subject.title: fix(approval): preserve Unicode in exec approval slug truncation

question: Should this PR be required to demonstrate a production non-UUID exec approval ID, or should arbitrary Unicode approval IDs become a supported shared-renderer contract?
rationale: Current production evidence points to UUID-generated exec IDs, while the proposed behavior is only demonstrated with a synthetic request; choosing to broaden the identifier contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Require reachable proof
options.body: Keep the existing UUID contract and merge this change only if a real Gateway or supported producer can emit a Unicode exec approval ID.

options.title: Generalize shared slugs
options.body: Explicitly support arbitrary approval IDs by moving Unicode-safe prefix generation into the shared approval renderer and testing exec and plugin surfaces together.

options.title: Decline defensive churn
options.body: Close the PR if exec IDs are intentionally UUID-only and no supported arbitrary-ID producer exists.

recommendation.title: Require reachable proof
recommendation.body: Keep the existing UUID contract and merge this change only if a real Gateway or supported producer can emit a Unicode exec approval ID.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared forwarder history makes this the strongest available owner for deciding whether the exec-ID contract should remain UUID-only.
